claims.text: The Ollama host is passed EXPLICITLY, per call. OLLAMA_HOST is neither read for routing nor written anywhere here
claims.why: The function takes ollama_host parameter and uses it; no reference to OLLAMA_HOST environment variable in this chunk.

claims.text: the local flag is a property of the RESOLVED host rather than of the provider's name: the bench is another machine, so a probe sent there is egress and is labelled as such on every record it produces.
claims.why: For local, lane is set to 'trusted' if _is_local_http(host) else 'untrusted'; the Lane's local flag is bool(getattr(a, 'local', False)), which is set by the adapter based on host.

claims.text: Subclasses the council's refusal ON PURPOSE. "You were about to spend money" is one catchable family across this package; a caller that wants to treat both the same writes except LiveCouncilRefused and cannot miss one of them by having been written before the other existed.
claims.why: class LiveCanaryRefused(LiveCouncilRefused) is declared; inheritance is as stated.

claims.text: Three places, because default_lanes is not the only way to build a Lane and a gate that only understood that one path would be a gate with a documented bypass: * the adapter field, set by default_lanes; * ask.__self__, for a bound method of an adapter; * ask.__closure__, which is where _bind keeps its adapter -- so a hand-rolled Lane(ask=_bind(ClaudeAdapter())) is caught too.
claims.why: The function checks lane.adapter, getattr(ask, '__self__', None), and iterates ask.__closure__ cells; all three sources are covered.

claims.text: Finding NOTHING means ask is a plain caller-supplied callable, and the verdict for that is deliberately the same one session.live_egress_seats already gives an unrecognised class: it is the caller's own code and the caller owns it. That is the single existing rule, applied here rather than re-decided.
claims.why: The function returns an empty tuple when no adapters found; the verdict is left to live_egress_seats on an empty sequence, which is the same as an unrecognised class.

claims.text: The classification itself is NOT done here -- it is session.live_egress_seats, imported. This function only resolves a lane back to its adapter(s) and prefixes the lane's identity onto whatever that one classifier says, so the canary and the council can never drift into disagreeing about which seats cost money.
claims.why: The function calls live_egress_seats(_adapters_behind(lane)) and prefixes lane.vendor/lane.model; it does not classify itself.

claims.text: refused_by_floor folds into error (the transport refused; no model was asked to be wrong).
The checker runs ONLY on status == "ok": grading the body of a reply we never received would manufacture a wrong_answer out of an outage, which is the same lie as merging the two statuses.
claims.why: grade checks if reply.status != 'ok' and returns error status; only when status is 'ok' does it call probe.check.

claims.text: Sequential within a lane on purpose: four concurrent calls to the same vendor is a load test, not a health check, and it would make the latency numbers -- the thing the trailing median compares -- meaningless. It is also what keeps a hung vendor to ONE occupied slot rather than four.
claims.why: _run_lane iterates probes sequentially in a for loop inside one thread; no concurrency within a lane.

claims.text: Threads are DAEMONS and are ABANDONED at the wall clock rather than joined: a thread cannot be killed, so a hung vendor must degrade the report instead of blocking it.
claims.why: Threads are created with daemon=True and joined with timeout max(0.0, deadline - time.monotonic()); they are not forcibly killed.

claims.text: Every abandoned (lane, probe) is still reported -- as timeout/wall_clock -- because a silently dropped row is indistinguishable from a probe that was never scheduled.
claims.why: After joining, results list is built from plan; if box.get('result') is None, a ProbeResult with status 'timeout' and reason 'wall_clock' is created.

claims.text: live is the SPEND OPT-IN and defaults to False. Any lane that still carries a shipped vendor transport (live_egress_lanes) raises LiveCanaryRefused here -- before the run id, before a nonce, before a thread, before one byte is dispatched, and therefore before there is anything for append_history to write.
claims.why: The check `if not live: seats = live_egress_lanes(lanes); if seats: raise LiveCanaryRefused` occurs before started, deadline, gate, run_id, threads, or any dispatch.

claims.text: Fake lanes are unaffected, so the offline harness never has to ask for permission it does not need.
claims.why: live_egress_lanes returns empty for lanes with no real adapters, so no exception is raised for fake lanes.

claims.text: Materialised ONCE, before anything inspects it: the gate below iterates the roster, and a one-shot iterator would arrive here full, be drained by the gate, and reach the scheduling loop empty -- a canary of no lanes, reported as if it had run.
claims.why: lanes = tuple(lanes) materialises the sequence before use; the gate iterates it later without consuming an iterator.

claims.text: FIRST, above everything: a refusal after the probes were built is still a refusal, but a refusal after dispatch is not one.
claims.why: The live check is before probe building or dispatch; probes are built after the check in the loop.

observations.what: run_canary raises LiveCanaryRefused before any dispatch, but the exception message includes lane seats; the message is constructed from live_egress_lanes output which is computed before the refusal.
_run_lane catches BaseException, which includes KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit; this is broader than Exception and may suppress user interrupts during a canary run.
The gate Semaphore is created with max(1, int(max_parallel)); if max_parallel is 0, it becomes 1, allowing at least one concurrent lane.

In run_canary, threads are started before the join loop; if a thread raises an unhandled exception, it will not be caught and could propagate to the main thread, but since daemon threads are used, the exception is printed to stderr but does not affect the main flow.

The grade function uses reply.model or lane.model; if reply.model is an empty string, it will fall back to lane.model, but if it is a non-empty string that is not a valid model, it will be used as is.

risks: _run_lane | medium | Catching BaseException may suppress KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit, making it hard for users to interrupt a canary run; should catch Exception instead. | Check if any code in the canary intentionally relies on catching BaseException.
